title: The High Priestess

seo.title: Destiny matrix 2 — The High Priestess: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: What arcanum 2 in the destiny matrix means: The High Priestess is an energy of instinct, silence and hidden knowledge, in a strong and a weak version.
queries: what does 2 mean in destiny matrix
meaning of arcanum 2 in the destiny matrix

meaning: The second arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of perception: not of action, but of taking in. If the first arcanum does things and announces itself, the second first reads the situation and only then decides whether it is worth showing up at all. The High Priestess is about knowledge that comes before any proof, and about the pause between the impulse and the deed, where understanding is born.

In character this is a quiet, receiving force — not pressure but sensitivity. The two thinks not in results but in pictures: out of pauses, tones of voice and small details it puts the whole together faster than it manages to justify it. From the inside it feels like “I just know” — the conclusion is ready, and the explanation for it is built on afterwards. In noise and bustle such a person goes deaf; in silence they hear.

The main engine of the two is the need to understand before taking part, and its conflict is hidden right there. Knowledge for it is a value to be guarded, not spent: it feels far too well how easily openness gets turned into vulnerability. So the energy of the number is balancing all the time on the edge of being closed — the same depth that gives protection is also able to lock a person inside themselves.

The strength of the two is defined by where its knowledge is aimed. In the mature form it turns what it perceives into work and shares it, and people come to it for understanding where everyone else is rushing to conclusions. In the weak one it stores up what it has seen: the picture of the world is assembled, but there is no taking part in that picture, and from the outside such closedness reads as coldness. The difference is not in the sharpness of the sensitivity, but in whether the knowledge goes out or stays a load nobody has asked for.

Within the deck the two differs from its neighbours by the direction of the energy. The first arcanum, The Magician, is active and turned outwards — it begins and creates movement; the two is turned inwards — it takes in and waits for its moment. The third, The Empress, takes the same inner knowledge and generously carries it out into the world, grows and feeds; at this step the two still keeps everything to itself. Its place in the row is the pause of attention between someone else’s action and one’s own answer: understand first, then show up.

article.title: Arcanum 2 in the destiny matrix — The High Priestess
article.short: Arcanum 2 in the destiny matrix is The High Priestess, the energy of knowing that comes before words. A person with a 2 hears the second layer of a conversation, holds the pause until the picture comes together, and can keep what they are told in confidence. It is the rarest arcanum in the matrix, and you can almost always spot it straight from the date of birth: a 2 belongs to people born on the 2nd of any month, in February, in the year 2000 or on 1 January.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 2 — The High Priestess: meaning, calling card, talent
seo.description: Destiny matrix 2 is The High Priestess, the rarest arcanum, read straight from your birth date: its calling card, talent and tasks, its strength and shadow.

sections.h2: What 2 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: Two comes straight after one, and the difference between them is the key to its meaning. One, The Magician, starts things: he declares, tries, pushes. Two takes things in first: it watches, listens, compares. Its main tool is perception. In a conversation, a person with a 2 hears two layers at once: what was said and what was meant. A pause before an answer, a phrase that is a little too smooth, a subject the other person steps around for the third time — out of small things like these the picture comes together for them before anyone has explained it.

The second quality of a 2 is the ability to hold. Someone else’s secret, a pause, your own opinion until the moment it is needed. In Arthur Waite’s divinatory meanings for The High Priestess, “mystery” and “wisdom” stand next to “silence” and “tenacity”. That is an important correction to the usual image: a 2 is quiet but not soft. It can go for months without arguing and still not give an inch.

The third is calm in the face of the unknown. Among the card’s meanings Waite also lists “the future as yet unrevealed”. A 2 does not need to know everything at once. It can live with “not clear yet”, does not rush the decision and waits for the situation to ripen. From outside this can look like slowness, though all the while information is being gathered.

The arcanum has a female name — The High Priestess, or simply the Priestess — but its meaning does not depend on gender. The numbers in the destiny matrix are calculated in the same way for men and women, and a man born in February has a 2 in the same point, meaning exactly the same thing. The High Priestess describes a way of knowing — through attention, without pressure — and anyone can have it.

sections.h2: 2 in the plus and in the minus

head: In the plus
In the minus
rows: Hears the subtext and notices what doesn’t add up
Takes a fragment for the whole: “I can see right through you”
Hoards what goes unsaid and waits for others to guess
Waits for complete certainty, and the moment slips away
Passes off anxiety as a premonition
Resists in silence, leaving nothing to argue about
Trades in knowledge: hints, gossip, playing both sides

paragraphs: The shadow of a 2 most often begins with silence. For weeks a person waits for those close to them to notice how tired they are, then snaps over an unwashed mug, and everyone is surprised: nothing was wrong, was it? Something was — it just never got said out loud. People with a 2 are sure that what matters is visible without words, because they see it themselves. Others cannot do that, and resentment over what went unguessed builds up on both sides.

Curiously, Waite did not see the opposite of The High Priestess as talkativeness at all. For him the reversed card means “passion, moral or physical ardour, conceit, surface knowledge”. In the matrix the card is never reversed, but the list is an exact description of the two ways a 2 breaks down. The first is ardour: when patience runs out, everything that has built up over months comes out at once, and it comes out sharply. The second is conceit: people with a 2 get so used to trusting their instinct that they stop checking. They read someone from two sentences and are sure they know everything about them, when that knowledge is precisely the surface kind.

The third shadow is knowledge as currency. Benebell Wen, author of the handbook Holistic Tarot, reads The High Priestess reversed as “deceit” and “duplicity”, with “disguises and concealment” that end up working against the one who hides. In life it looks familiar: “I know, but I won’t say”, information handed out piece by piece to gain influence, talking to each side of a conflict in its own language. The gift of seeing what is hidden is the same — it has simply been turned into an instrument of power.

sections.h2: Where a 2 appears in the matrix: check your date of birth
paragraphs: 2 is the rarest arcanum in the destiny matrix. Only 13.4% of people have it anywhere at all in their full reading; for the other arcana the share ranges from 13.8% to 85%. The reason is arithmetic, explained in the next section. The upshot is handy: to find out whether you have a 2 and where it stands, you hardly need a calculator.

head: You were born
Where your 2 stands
Share of people
rows: the [calling card](/encyclopedia/position/day) — point A; the physics of Sahasrara; the decade 0–10

the [spiritual task](/encyclopedia/position/month) — point B; the start of the [line of talent](/encyclopedia/position/profession); the first [task of the sky line](/encyclopedia/position/soul_tasks); the energy of Sahasrara; the decade 20–30
the [material task](/encyclopedia/position/year) — point C; [body resource](/encyclopedia/position/body_resource); the physics of Muladhara; the decade 40–50

the [spiritual male family line](/encyclopedia/position/father_line) — point F; [gifts of the family line](/encyclopedia/position/family_gifts); [parents and children](/encyclopedia/position/parents_children); the emotions of Sahasrara; the decade 10–20

paragraphs: Another 1.7% of people, born on other days, get a 2 only in the totals row of the [chakra map](/encyclopedia/position/chakras): the sum of a column’s seven numbers sometimes tips over a hundred, and 101 reduces to 1 + 0 + 1 = 2.

These cases overlap. People born on 2 February get a 2 twice — in the calling card and in the spiritual task. That does not double its force: one theme works in two roles, in full view of others and in inner work. And 2 February 2000 is the only date since 1900 with a 2 in three corners at once: A, B and C. One more detail: more than half of all people with a 2 in their matrix were born in February.

sections.h2: Why a 2 never appears in the centre of the matrix or in the karmic tail
paragraphs: Almost every point of the matrix, apart from the date itself, is produced by addition. The centre is the sum of the four corners; the karmic tail, the money and relationship lines and the purposes are sums of sums. If a result is above 22, its digits are added: 23 → 5, 30 → 3, 99 → 18. A two-digit number above 22 reduces this way to something between 3 and 18, and it never yields a 2. So in a point that is a sum, a 2 can only come from 1 + 1 (sums over a hundred occur only in the totals of the chakra map). And a 1 among the terms exists only for people born on the 1st or in January. Hence the only sum that gives a 2 is A + B for people born on 1 January: point F, and with it the emotions of Sahasrara.

That is why, in Natalia Ladini’s classic scheme, a 2 never appears in the centre, in the karmic task D or the karmic tail, in the money and relationship lines, in the point under the heart, in the inner points, in the spiritual female family line G, in the material family lines H and I, in the programs, or in any of the four purposes. If somewhere you were shown a 2 in one of these points, it was calculated by other rules. The same rule checks the birthday too: in this scheme the 24th gives 2 + 4 = 6, so the calling card of people born on the 24th is The Lovers, not The High Priestess.

sections.h2: 2 as the calling card: born on the 2nd
paragraphs: The calling card is point A, the birth day arcanum: what people pick up in the first minutes of meeting you. With a 2, the first impression is a quiet one. The person listens more than they talk, asks follow-up questions and says little about themselves. People trust them easily: on a train, in a queue, at a new job, it is to them that someone, half an hour in, pours out what they have never told their own family. Meanwhile they remain a mystery themselves — they have learned a great deal about the other person and said two sentences about themselves.

In a meeting, someone with a 2 in the calling card is often the last to speak, and a single remark from them turns the discussion. In a conflict they are called in as the third party: they are in no hurry to take sides and do not repeat to one side what they heard from the other. That is how they earn a reputation as someone you can tell.

The shadow of this calling card is opacity. Inside, the picture came together long ago; outside, nothing shows, and people cannot tell where they stand. Reserve is read as coldness or arrogance, silence in a meeting as disagreement. Hence the comments a person with a 2 hears all their life: “I can never tell with you”, “you keep everything to yourself”, “what are you thinking right now?”

Two simple things help. The first is to give people a little of yourself without waiting to be asked: one sentence about what you think removes half the guesswork about you. The second is to say what you have noticed in good time. If by the second week of a project you can see it is heading the wrong way, saying so that same day is worth more than a flawlessly accurate “I knew it” three months later.

sections.h2: 2 in the spiritual task and the line of talent: born in February
paragraphs: Everyone born in February has a 2 in point B. This is the most common way to meet The High Priestess, and in the reading she works in several roles at once: B is the spiritual task, B opens the line of talent, and B starts the sky line in the section on tasks of the soul.

The energy of point B shows early, so it is easy to take it for an ordinary character trait. From childhood a February 2 knows who in the group is upset with whom, and can tell from the face of someone unwrapping a present that they don’t like it, before the “thank you” is even out. They are rarely wrong about people.

The task begins where this gift stops being a pleasant quirk and becomes a responsibility. It has three parts. Trust your perception and don’t brush it off with “I must have imagined it”. Bring it out into the open: an understanding that is never voiced helps neither you nor anyone else. And tell knowledge from fear, because anxiety, too, can speak in a quiet, confident voice.

The line of talent has three points: B, P and K. A 2 occurs only in the first of them; it never appears in the middle point or in the inner point of talent. So a 2 sets the raw material of talent — the way a person grasps their material — while the form in which the talent earns money is decided by the other two arcana of the line. The raw material of a 2 is this: attention to details and inconsistencies, a memory for who said what and in what tone, an ear for the second layer in a text or a conversation. In a psychological reading, Wen links The High Priestess precisely to memory — to “how we encode, store, and retrieve our experiences”.

This raw material is paid for wherever someone needs to understand what does not lie on the surface. Analysis and research, checking and auditing, editing and translation, interviewing and recruitment, one-to-one consulting, investigative journalism, archives and museums, technical support, where a couple of lines in a log reveal the cause of a failure. All these jobs share one result: the client gains an understanding they did not have before. A 2 has a harder time where people are paid for volume: cold calling, selling from a stage, working on camera without preparation.

The trap of this talent is a hunch in place of verification. A 2 has strong instincts, and it is tempting to pass them off as conclusions. What makes them a professional is the moment an observation takes a form that can be checked: a report, a recommendation, the cause of a breakdown tracked down, a text that survives a fact-check.

sections.h2: 2 in the material task: born in 2000
paragraphs: Point C is calculated from the digits of the birth year: 2 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 2. Of all the years since 1900, only one works out like this, so a 2 in the material task is the mark of a generation: everyone born in 2000 has it, and nobody else does.

The material task is where a person’s qualities meet money, deadlines and things. A 2 here says that a reliable result comes through knowledge and precision, while pressure and sheer volume work less well. Money comes for what the person understands better than others: for expertise, for an error found, for careful work that never has to be redone. Ventures that take a long time to ripen go best, while sprints to get a result by Friday are draining and rarely pay off.

The difficulty here is invisibility. A 2 does good work quietly, waits for others to appreciate it and does not name a price. The work is there, but the money and recognition fall short of what it is worth. The practical lesson of the material task is to show what you have done and to be the first to state your terms: “Here’s what I found, and here’s what it costs.”

The same 2 stands in the section on body resource and in the physics of Muladhara, the row about everyday grounding. A person with it gets their strength back in quiet and solitude: a walk without headphones, water, music without words, a task you do on your own. A sign that the reserve is running low is irritation with people you usually put up with easily. The card speaks about what fills a person up and says nothing about how their body is doing.

sections.h2: 2 in the family line: born on 1 January
paragraphs: This is the rarest case — about 0.3% of people. Point F, the spiritual male family line, is calculated as A + B. For people born on 1 January both the day and the month are ones, The Magician and The Magician, and their sum is The High Priestess. On the chart itself, this is the only point where a 2 is produced by addition.

F holds not the character of a particular father but the principle of the male branch: what it held to be right and what it leaned on when there was nothing else to lean on. It works for a person of any gender. With a 2 the principle sounds like this: first understand, then act; don’t waste words; keep your word and other people’s secrets.

In the section on gifts of the family line, this reads as a ready resource: a clear head when everyone around is making noise, a feel for people in negotiations, the ability to stay silent about what isn’t yours to tell. In the section on relationships with parents and children, it reads as a family script with its own shadow: where silence is valued, the most important things can go unsaid for years. The task is to keep the ability to listen and to start naming out loud what the family is used to stepping around.

sections.h2: 2 across the decades and in the chakra map
paragraphs: The reading by decades divides life up to 80 into eight stretches, and for each of the four groups a 2 leads a different one. It is the backdrop of the stretch, not a forecast of events.

head: Decade
Who lives it under a 2
What this stretch can be like
rows: the child as observer: watches the others play for a long time before joining in, and notices more in the family than anyone tells them
growing up through inner work: books, a diary, one close friend instead of a big crowd
gathering and slow choosing while peers loudly try everything going; the trap is preparation that stretches out for years
for them this is the 2040s: the stretch when experience turns into expertise that people come looking for

paragraphs: In the chakra map a 2 most often stands in [Sahasrara](/encyclopedia/chakra/sahasrara), the row about values and meaning. For people born on the 2nd it is in the physics, that is, in what a person does: they arrive at their convictions through observation, and other people’s sermons do not convince them. For those born in February it is in the energy, in what drives them: the need to understand how things really work leads them to meaning. For people born on 1 January it is in the emotions: a quiet sense of inner certainty goes with the path they have chosen. For those born in 2000 the 2 is the physics of [Muladhara](/encyclopedia/chakra/muladhara), the row of everyday grounding: home as a closed, quiet place, a habit of looking after one’s resources and not putting them on display.

sections.h2: Living with a 2: five working habits

ol: **A hunch journal.** Write each premonition down in one line with the date, and a month later mark whether it came true. After twenty entries you can see where your instinct hits the mark and where anxiety is speaking in its voice.

**Tell instinct from anxiety by how it sounds.** Instinct is usually specific and calm: “this contractor is going to miss the deadline.” Anxiety is vague and urgent: “everything’s going to go wrong, I have to do something right now.” The first is worth checking; the second is worth waiting out.

**The 24-hour rule.** If you notice something important, say it within a day, in one sentence and without proof: “I think something’s off here — let’s check.” A small observation is easy to voice; one you have been carrying for six months is almost impossible.
**A question instead of a conclusion.** Before deciding what someone thinks and wants, ask them. A 2 guesses right often, but not always, and the costliest mistakes are the ones you were sure about.

**Silence in your schedule.** The perception of a 2 goes deaf in noise. Time every day without conversation, a feed or background sound is a working tool: without it, perception goes dull before your strength runs out.

paragraphs.h3: With the people closest to you

paragraphs: A 2 never appears on the relationship line, but a person with it in the calling card or the spiritual task brings it into any couple. They sense their partner’s mood from the way the front door was closed, and they know how to be there without unnecessary words. They need space: press them and they withdraw into themselves. The main rule for such a couple is that wishes are said out loud. A 2 is sure that what matters is visible anyway, while the partner most likely sees it less clearly than the 2 believes.

sections.h2: 2 and its look-alikes: how not to mix them up
paragraphs: Five arcana are most often confused with 2: all of them are in some way about knowledge, silence or what is hidden.

head: Arcanum
How it resembles 2
How it differs
rows: neighbours in the sequence, both about beginnings
The Magician creates outwardly and says “I can”; The High Priestess works inwardly and says “I see”
both are female arcana at the start of the sequence
The Empress grows what can be seen and cares for it; The High Priestess understands and keeps what is hidden

The Hierophant teaches by the rules and explains, The High Priestess knows and does not explain; for Waite he is “the ruling power of external religion”, she “the prevailing genius of the esoteric, withdrawn power”
for Waite The Hermit is a card of attainment, an understanding reached that becomes a beacon for others; The High Priestess knows and keeps that knowledge to herself
both are about what is hidden

for Wen The High Priestess is “personal mystery”, knowledge a person keeps to themselves, while The Moon is “concealed environmental forces”, mirages and fears; a 2 says “I know, but I’m keeping quiet”, The Moon says “I don’t know, and it makes me uneasy”

paragraphs: What happens when both arcana stand in one matrix is covered on the combination pages: [The Magician and The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/combination/1-2), [The High Priestess and The Empress](/encyclopedia/combination/2-3), [The High Priestess and The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/2-5), [The High Priestess and The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/2-9), [The High Priestess and The Moon](/encyclopedia/combination/2-18).

sections.h2: Waite’s High Priestess: the pillars, the scroll and the veil
paragraphs: In Arthur Waite’s deck, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith in 1909, The High Priestess sits between two pillars: a dark one with the letter B and a light one with the letter J. These are Boaz and Jachin, the two bronze pillars at the entrance to Solomon’s temple in the First Book of Kings (in the Douay–Rheims Bible, the Third Book of Kings). The names are usually translated as “in it is strength” and “he shall establish”. Waite calls them the pillars “of the mystic Temple”, and The High Priestess sits at its entrance, between black and white. Two is the number of the pair, and on this card the pair is drawn quite literally.

Behind her hangs the veil of the Temple, “embroidered with palms and pomegranates”. The veil screens the sanctuary, and the card does not show what lies beyond it; Wen notes only that behind the priestess there is “a body of calm water”. Palms and pomegranates are temple images too: in the Bible’s description of Solomon’s temple, palm trees are carved on its walls, pomegranates adorn the capitals of those very pillars, and pomegranates are embroidered on the hem of the high priest’s robe as well. A pomegranate keeps hundreds of seeds under one smooth skin — it is itself a picture of what this card is about.

In her hands is a scroll inscribed TORA, its edge covered by her mantle. Waite explains both details. Tora here signifies “the Greater Law, the Secret Law and the second sense of the Word”. And the mantle covers part of the scroll “to shew that some things are implied and some spoken”. You will not find a shorter definition of 2: the second sense, what stands behind what is said. Wen adds a play on words: in Japanese, tora means “tiger”. The High Priestess is still, but it is the stillness of a crouching tiger, not of sleep.

At her feet is the lunar crescent; on her head is a horned diadem with a globe in the middle, in which Wen sees three phases of the moon: waxing, full and waning. On her breast is a large solar cross. Waite’s vestments are “flowing and gauzy”, and Wen notices that at the bottom her gown “seems to have transformed to water”. Waite calls The High Priestess “the Queen of the borrowed light” and adds at once: “but this is the light of all”.

A detail that is missing from the card matters too. Comparing The High Priestess with The Hierophant, Waite writes that The Hierophant gives the sign “distinguishing between the manifest and concealed part of doctrine”, whereas “the High Priestess makes no sign”. He teaches; she does not explain. Waite has one more scene, about The Chariot: if the victor in the chariot came to the pillars of the Temple where The High Priestess is seated, “he could not open the scroll called Tora, nor if she questioned him could he answer”. Outward victory does not open the way to this knowledge.

In older decks the card was called the Papess — La Papesse in the Marseille tarot — and was linked to the legend of Pope Joan, a woman said to have secretly become pope. Waite rejected the reading “Pope’s Wife” as “opposed to the symbolism” and would not see her as “Occult Science on the threshold of the Sanctuary of Isis”. For him The High Priestess is “the Secret Church” and the Shekinah — in Kabbalah, the presence of God in the world. “When he reads the Law she gives the Divine meaning,” Waite writes of the just man, and concludes that “there are some respects in which this card is the highest and holiest of the Greater Arcana”.

If 2 has come up as your arcanum of the year, that is a separate story: a High Priestess year is a time to gather, observe and choose your moment. The details are on the page [2 for the year in the destiny matrix](/year/2).

The High Priestess in combination with every arcanum: [The Magician](/encyclopedia/combination/1-2), [The Empress](/encyclopedia/combination/2-3), [The Emperor](/encyclopedia/combination/2-4), [The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/2-5), [The Lovers](/encyclopedia/combination/2-6), [The Chariot](/encyclopedia/combination/2-7), [Justice](/encyclopedia/combination/2-8), [The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/2-9), [The Wheel of Fortune](/encyclopedia/combination/2-10), [Strength](/encyclopedia/combination/2-11), [The Hanged Man](/encyclopedia/combination/2-12), [Death](/encyclopedia/combination/2-13), [Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/2-14), [The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/2-15), [The Tower](/encyclopedia/combination/2-16), [The Star](/encyclopedia/combination/2-17), [The Moon](/encyclopedia/combination/2-18), [The Sun](/encyclopedia/combination/2-19), [Judgement](/encyclopedia/combination/2-20), [The World](/encyclopedia/combination/2-21), [The Fool](/encyclopedia/combination/2-22).

If you were looking for a destiny matrix for two people, that is a different calculation: compatibility, where the matching points of two personal matrices are added together. A 2 is even rarer there. By Yuliana Lisovskaya’s calculation it is possible in only two points, and only when both partners have ones there: if both were born on the 1st (the point about how others see the couple) or both in January (the point about why the couple met). Such a couple keeps a great deal to themselves, and they meet in order to learn to talk about their feelings instead of storing them up. More on the page [“2 in compatibility”](/encyclopedia/compatibility/2).
